title: English Language Proficiency; Out of Service Criteria
key_claim: FMCSA proposes to write English language proficiency noncompliance into the out-of-service criteria, disclosing that 60,399 ELP violations were issued between 25 June 2025 and 19 March 2026 with 19,045 resulting in out-of-service orders, with a carve-out for trips inside the US-Mexico border commercial zones; comments closed 9 October 2026.
frame_summary: FMCSA argues that English-proficiency violations are a roadside safety matter best enforced through out-of-service orders, and proposes to harden the June 2025 enforcement practice into standing regulation, with a carve-out for the US-Mexico border commercial zones.
verbatim_quote: Between June 25, 2025 and March 19, 2026, there were 60,399 ELP violations issued, with 19,045 of those resulting in OOS orders.
verbatim_list: Comments must be received on or before October 9, 2026.

The 19,045 ELP violations that resulted in OOS orders all occurred outside of border commercial zones, while the remaining 44,354 ELP violations that occurred in border commercial zones did not result in OOS orders.
notes: Notice of proposed rulemaking, 91 FR 51422, Docket FMCSA-2026-0826, responding to a CVSA petition; would codify the out-of-service practice in force since 25 June 2025. The regulatory analysis section carries the enforcement counts used in the scan. title: Letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on non-domiciled CDL restrictions and California transportation funds
key_claim: Senator Adam Schiff and California colleagues estimate the non-domiciled CDL rule will sideline about 194,000 lawfully authorised drivers, protest the withholding of $160 million in FY2027 National Highway Performance Program funds from California, and ask DOT to rescind the rule.
frame_summary: The senators argue the rule and the California funding withholding are punitive measures unsupported by crash data, warning they sideline an estimated 194,000 lawful drivers and threaten a supply chain crisis that raises consumer prices.
verbatim_quote: The Department’s rule will sideline an estimated 194,000 experienced drivers with authorization to work lawfully, effectively making our roads less safe and potentially creating a supply chain crisis that will most likely make everyday goods less affordable for Americans.
verbatim_list: Reducing the pool of qualified drivers will therefore increase shipping costs and place upward pressure on prices for groceries, furniture, and other essential goods.
withholding $160 million in FY2027 National Highway Performance Program funds from California
notes: Structural anchor: the canonical quantified statement of the driver-pool scale at stake and the congressional counter-case, published 11/06/2026, inside the 3-6 month band. title: Trucking Industry Forecast for 2027
key_claim: ACT Research frames 2027 as better demand signals meeting a limited capacity response: September dry van spot rates excluding fuel were $2.16 a mile, 33% above a year earlier, aggregate contract rates $2.52 excluding fuel, up 18% year over year, while September Class 8 net orders fell 7% year over year.
frame_summary: ACT Research frames 2027 as better demand meeting a limited capacity response: firm pricing with the supply side constrained by replacement economics, financing and driver availability rather than any single rule.

title: DAT: Truckload rates rise in September as diesel tops $6 a gallon
key_claim: September dry van spot rates averaged $3.01 a mile including fuel, up 12 cents from August and up 96 cents year over year, as the monthly national average diesel price surpassed $6 for the first time at $6.291 a gallon; net of fuel, van linehaul fell 2 cents to $2.17 and the van Truckload Volume Index was down 1% year over year.
frame_summary: DAT frames September's rate rise as a diesel story: record fuel prices lifted all-in rates while van linehaul slipped and volumes softened, implying pass-through rather than scarcity.

title: TL linehaul rates up 10% in September, shipment counts remain positive
key_claim: The September 2026 Cass data show the Truckload Linehaul Index up 10.1% year over year while Cass shipments rose 1.9% year over year and expenditures jumped 20.4%, with the article reading the dataset as confirming the impact of strict regulatory enforcement on non-compliant capacity.
frame_summary: FreightWaves reads the September Cass data as confirmation that regulatory enforcement is removing non-compliant capacity and that carriers enter the bid season in a position of strength.
verbatim_quote: Cass’ TL linehaul index, which tracks rates excluding fuel and accessorial surcharges, increased 10.1% year over year
verbatim_list: Freight shipments recorded by Cass increased 1.9% y/y in September.
Cass’ expenditures index, which measures total freight spend including fuel, jumped 20.4% y/y (up 6.7% sequentially).
The dataset confirms the impact strict regulatory enforcement is having on non-compliant capacity.
notes: By Todd Maiden, FreightWaves finance editor, covering the Cass Transportation Index Report for September 2026 (Cass Information Systems with ACT Research). title: North America Truckload Freight Market Update: October 2026
key_claim: C.H. Robinson's October 2026 truckload update reports route-guide failures rising again as capacity tightens, says federal enforcement actions tied to commercial driver licenses, visas and English-language proficiency are expected to further reduce the available driver pool, and holds its dry van cost per mile forecasts at +30% year over year for 2026 and +10% for 2027.
frame_summary: C.H. Robinson tells shippers that rising route-guide failures mark genuine tightening and that federal enforcement on licences, visas and English proficiency will further shrink the driver pool, holding its +30% 2026 and +10% 2027 cost forecasts.
verbatim_quote: Federal enforcement actions tied to commercial driver licenses, visas, and English-language proficiency, for example, are expected to further reduce the available driver pool.
verbatim_list: The C.H. Robinson 2026 dry van cost per mile forecast remains at +30% year over year (y/y), while the 2027 forecast remains at +10% y/y.
Driver recruiting and retention remain the industry's top challenge
